title: Prove GitHub request lifetime and shared ownership in Node Vitest

intentCoverage.report:
Verdict: Caught

Story: SEED-413#github-request-lifetime-and-evidence-via-vitest
Revision: 3968e1fa31430f4661c5c1ffcfe80b9250ffe6ab
Promise: the last departure of a shared pinned GitHub read ends that read's child process.

The maintained poll caught the fault. In `dashboard/backend-tests/observation/authenticated-read-owned-lifetime.spec.ts`, the test "the last departure releases the pinned read and a later request asks again" failed at `expect.poll(() => processAlive(pid), { timeout: 5_000 }).toBe(false)` (lines 131–133). `processAlive` from `dashboard/test-support/support/processGroup.ts` kept returning true, so the matcher timed out with `expected true to be false`. The test did not reach `childExitedBy()` being `SIGTERM`.

Fault: in production `Distribution/src/skills/dough-execute-plan/scripts/github-request-outstanding.mjs`, `OutstandingReads.waitFor`, when the last waiter left (`outstanding.waiters === 0`), the edit skipped `outstanding.controller.abort(waiter.reason)`. That abort is what releases the shared read's signal; Node then SIGTERMs the owned `gh` child. The outstanding-map removal (`#ended`) stayed. Test assertions and fixtures were unchanged.

Scratch checkout: `/tmp/dough-intent-coverage-3968e1fa`, detached at `3968e1fa31430f4661c5c1ffcfe80b9250ffe6ab`, outside the execution checkout. Pre-probe status: not on any branch, nothing to commit, working tree clean. `node_modules` was a clone of the execution checkout's install because `package-lock.json` matched that revision. Removed after the restored pass: `/tmp/dough-intent-coverage-3968e1fa`.

Command, three times:
PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH" caffeinate -s -i npm run test:dashboard:backend -- dashboard/backend-tests/observation/authenticated-read-owned-lifetime.spec.ts --workers=1

1. Baseline, before the fault. Exit 0. Vitest duration 3.36s, start 22:14:23. Both tests passed. The last-departure test passed in 147ms.
2. Faulted. Exit 1. Vitest duration 6.05s, start 22:14:57. The one-departure test passed in 147ms. The last-departure test failed in 5078ms because `processAlive(pid)` stayed true through the 5s poll. Teardown also reported `error during close`: a GitHub call was seen without that test's request owner. The catch is the `processAlive` poll.
3. Restored. Exit 0. Vitest duration 1.06s, start 22:15:20. Both tests passed. The last-departure test passed in 148ms.

Reach: the baseline passed this same last-departure test, so the run reached the child-end poll before any fault. After the fault, that test again passed the earlier checks that the child was alive after the first departure, then failed only once the last waiter had left. The sibling test still passed, so a departure that leaves a waiter still left the child running.

Wrong behavior: after the last waiter left, and while the held GitHub answer was still unreleased, the pinned read's `gh` child stayed alive. The poll observed that directly.

Restoration: `git checkout` put the abort back. Tracked diff was empty and HEAD stayed `3968e1fa31430f4661c5c1ffcfe80b9250ffe6ab`. Ignored leftovers were `dashboard/backend-tests/test-results/` and the probe `node_modules/` copy. The restored command passed. The worktree was then removed. The execution checkout stayed at `489d36d1a027b1203366ac5eca2574a6e13bbdf9` and was not edited.

Next proof action: none for this promise on the observed last-departure path. This probe does not call for a stronger assertion or a new test there.

No already-planned repair or prior disposition was matched during this check.
